# `bin/new-run`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/new-run`](../../../bin/new-run)

## What it says about itself

```text
bin/new-run WORKSPACE SLUG --role solver [--problem NAME] [--input PATH ...] [--input-approved PATH ...]
   bin/new-run WORKSPACE SLUG --role referee --claim SOLVER_RUN ID [--question certify|hypotheses|sentence]
                                                                   [--input PATH ...]
   bin/new-run WORKSPACE SLUG --role evaluator --input data/locked/... [--input PATH ...]
   bin/new-run WORKSPACE SLUG --role other
   every role: [--cpu-hours H] [--threads N] [--mem-gb G] [--harness claude-net|codex|codex-net] [--module NAME ...]

Creates WORKSPACE/runs/NNN-SLUG/{BRIEF.md,input/,scratch/,output/} with NNN = 1 + the highest
run number across all workspaces (run names are unique project-wide). NNN is added by this tool:
pass the slug alone ("s9-read", not "087-s9-read"); a slug that starts with digits and a hyphen is refused.
--harness claude-net|codex|codex-net copies the matching harness note to RUN/HARNESS-NOTE.md, which
bin/run-external requires for --via codex and for --network (LESSONS.md "Networked and Codex launches need their flags bound"). Writes a BRIEF.md
skeleton for the role; the orchestrator fills the ⟨slots⟩ before the user's gate.

Refuses to copy anything from data/locked/, any record file (LEDGER.log, CLAIMS.md, HANDOFF.md,
ORCHESTRATOR.md, CLAUDE.md, another BRIEF.md), and for a solver anything from another run
(solvers never see prior attempts) unless the user excepted the file by name: --input-approved. A referee gets exactly: input/claim.json (the one claim),
input/artifact/... (that claim's artifact and its declared deps), input/PROBLEM.md, input/ledger-premises.md when the
claim has `ledger` premises (bin/claims-extract --ids; LESSONS.md "A referee is given the ledger entries a claim rests on"),
and nothing else (--input is refused for a referee); its question, claim and the bytes it was given are recorded in
data/referee-bindings/<run>.json, outside every run (P-12 C3: the earned tag reads them from there, never from the run).
--input-approved needs the file's bytes on the user's exceptions list, data/packet-exceptions.json (! bin/packet-except).
A solver also gets input/validate-claims.py. Every run gets RUN/.limits (--cpu-hours, --threads, --mem-gb: enforced by
the hook and bin/limits-exec), and with --module, RUN/.modules (a licence module of kit-env.json; bin/run-external
--module must match it). An evaluator is the only role that may receive data/locked/ inputs
(label maps, answer keys); it emits scores only. Prints the bin/run-external launch line (LESSONS.md "Every worker is a headless main process":
no worker is launched as a subagent).
```
